title: Japan Campervan — Hokkaido Powder Belt
subtitle: 雪・車・山 — snow, van, mountains · one van, one island, chase the storm
coverCredit: Mt Yotei from the Niseko slopes
summary: Fly to Sapporo, pick up a campervan, chase snow. No fixed bookings except the van — the weather decides where we ride. Hokkaido's powder belt stretches from the **Niseko volcano cluster** in the southwest up the central spine to the **Daisetsuzan range** in the northeast: one logical road trip. Niseko, Rusutsu, Kiroro, Kokusai, then up past Furano and Kamui to Asahidake. Two missions make the trip: **climbing Mt Yotei** and the **Asahidake volcanic bowls**.

features.title: The powder belt — the best snow on Earth
features.description: Hokkaido's annual snowfall is measured in **metres**: Niseko averages 15 m, Kiroro is Japan's snowiest resort at 21 m. The powder belt runs from the Niseko volcano cluster in the southwest up the central spine to the Daisetsuzan range in the northeast — one logical road trip, and the campervan makes it work: you sleep at the resort car park, wake up first in line, and follow the storm. The honest bit: van nights are cold (we'll have a proper heater), no toilet on board (onsens and service stations are legendary), and we sleep at ski-resort lots and onsen towns — exactly how the locals do it.

features.title: One van, one island, ~700 km of snow
features.description: Fly into **New Chitose (CTS)**, pick up a winter campervan (4WD, studless tyres, diesel heater) and drive the powder belt southwest → northeast. The spine is fixed; the daily stops are decided by the **snow forecast** — that's the whole point of the van. Late January, 10–12 days.

features.title: Yotei & Asahidake — the reason we go
features.description:
Two full alpine days that no lift ticket can buy.

**Mt Yotei** — "Hokkaido's Fuji", 1,898 m, a perfect stratovolcano. We climb it on our own skin track from the Niseko side: ~6 h up, wind-loaded faces, a summit view over the whole volcano, and a proper line back down. Needs a clear weather window.

**Asahidake** — ropeway to 1,600 m on Hokkaido's highest peak in the Daisetsuzan range. Volcanic bowls and steaming vents, terrain you can't get anywhere else. Both need a **splitboard + skins + transceiver/probe/shovel per person**.

features.title: Campervan + the Powder Belt pass
features.description: The "Powder Belt" is a proven product: **Hoshino Resorts sells a Hokkaido Powder Belt Campervan Plan** — campervan (Robinson 771/106: 4WD, studless tyres, FF heater, ETC) + **5-day lift pass for Tomamu + Furano + Kamui** + breakfast/sauna/waxing at Tomamu & OMO7 Asahikawa, pickup at New Chitose. From ~¥215,300 (~€1,300) per van for 4n/5d — the hybrid van+hotel loop that makes January nights comfortable. **Book 3–4 months out** (January is Hokkaido's busiest foreign-visitor month).

Belgian licence: JAF official translation (no IDP needed for BE)
Splitboard: buy/rent (Jones Stratos) + Gentemstick Barracuda for resort days
Avalanche gear per person: transceiver + probe + shovel + training
Pass check: Powder Belt 5-day pass vs day tickets (Tomamu/Furano/Kamui)

practical.notes: **Licence**: Belgian licence + official JAF translation (¥4,000) — NO international permit needed for Belgium (Dutch licences need the IDP). **Driving**: left-hand traffic, studless winter tyres standard, 4WD varies by model — confirm at booking. **Van life**: FF diesel heater, keep the exhaust vent clear of snow (CO safety), free overnight parking at resort lots + michi-no-eki + onsen towns. **Onsen**: wash before you soak, no swimwear, ask about tattoos. **Food**: konbini breakfasts, ramen lunches, hotpot dinners — ~¥3,000–5,000/day pp. **Weather windows**: January storms come in pulses — some days we ride lifts, some we earn turns, some we eat ramen and wait for the next one. That's the adventure.

days.title: Fly to New Chitose → pick up the van
days.notes: Day 1 of 10. Land CTS (afternoon), shuttle to the campervan office, pick up the van: 4WD, studless tyres, FF heater. First konbini haul, then a quick drive towards Sapporo.

blocks.title: Campervan pickup
blocks.description: Hoshino Powder Belt plan or Campervan Inc. — CTS pickup, shuttle timed to arrival. Book 3–4 months out.

blocks.title: First Hokkaido ramen
blocks.description: Sapporo miso ramen — the city invented it.

days.title: Sapporo warm-up — Teine, Bankei, Kokusai
days.notes: Legs first, legs fresh. Teine is the 1972 Olympic venue with night skiing; Bankei is a tiny local hill with a night park; Sapporo Kokusai (40 min) gets ~3 m of high-season snow. Night sessions in the city, then the best ramen in Japan.

blocks.title: Teine full day + night session
blocks.description: 1972 Olympic venue, minutes from the city, night skiing under the lights.

blocks.title: Sapporo Kokusai
blocks.description: ~3 m high-season snow, 40 min from the city. Or Bankei for a cheap night park.

days.title: Niseko — Grand Hirafu
days.notes: The powder heartland. Grand Hirafu first — the most famous powder resort on Earth for a reason. Storm map decides the rest of the week: Rusutsu, Kiroro, or back to Kokusai.

blocks.title: Grand Hirafu
blocks.description: Sidecountry gates off the top, Hanazono trees when it's deep. The van sleeps at the bottom of the gondola.

blocks.title: First onsen + kaisen-don
blocks.description: Kutchan or Hirafu — seafood bowl and a soak after day one.

days.title: Rusutsu & Kiroro — wherever the storm hits
days.notes: Open day. Rusutsu: empty glades and a resort that feels like a theme park. Kiroro: Japan's snowiest resort, 21 m a year. Both ~1h from Hirafu. The forecast decides — that's the whole point of the van.

blocks.title: Rusutsu
blocks.description: Isola and East mountains, glades for days, almost no queues.

blocks.title: Kiroro
blocks.description: 21 m of annual snowfall — the deepest resort in Japan. Peak-side trees when it's nuking.

days.title: Open day — storm chase or Yotei scouting
days.notes: Wildcard day. Options: (a) one more Niseko-area powder day wherever the storm is, (b) scout the Yotei approach + soak at an onsen town, (c) start the drive north early. Decide by breakfast.

blocks.title: Things to decide
blocks.description: Yotei weather window (needs clear), whether Mt Racey breaks the drive north, and where the first central-spine day goes.

blocks.title: Yotei scouting
blocks.description: Check the Annupuri-side approach and the snowpack. The mission day needs a window.

days.title: Mt Yotei mission
days.notes: The reason we came. Skin up Hokkaido's Fuji (1,898 m) from the Niseko side — ~6 h up, wind-loaded faces on the way down, summit view over the whole volcano. Splitboard + skins + transceiver/probe/shovel. Clear-day only.

blocks.title: Yotei skin track
blocks.description: Start from the Annupuri side early. 6–8 h round trip. Check the forecast — this is a weather-window day.

days.title: Up the spine — Mt Racey → Furano
days.notes: North towards the central spine. Mt Racey (Yubari) breaks the drive: huge dumps (~8 m+), 40% advanced, one gondola, closest Japow to the airport. Then Furano: classic powder and tree runs, far fewer people than Niseko.

blocks.title: Mt Racey
blocks.description: Huge dumps, Indy Pass resort, breaks the drive north.

blocks.title: Furano
blocks.description: Central belt: drier snow, tree runs, best when Niseko is tracked out. On the Powder Belt pass.

days.title: Kamui Ski Links — Asahikawa's secret
days.notes: 'Hokkaido's best-kept secret': 25 courses, ~600 m vertical, famous back bowls + sidecountry, cheap — and part of the Hoshino Powder Belt pass. 30 min from Asahikawa. A proper hidden-gem day.

blocks.title: Kamui Ski Links
blocks.description: Back bowls + sidecountry, cheap lift tickets, almost no queues. Powder Belt pass covers it.

blocks.title: Asahikawa ramen
blocks.description: The shio-ramen capital — a different bowl than Sapporo's miso.

days.title: Asahidake mission
days.notes: Ropeway to 1,600 m on Hokkaido's highest peak, in the Daisetsuzan range. Volcanic bowls and steaming vents — terrain you can't get anywhere else. Backcountry: beacon, probe, shovel.

blocks.title: Asahidake bowls
blocks.description: Ropeway to 1,600 m, then it's all you. The famous fumarole zone steams at the base.

days.title: Flex morning → fly home
days.notes: Wildcard morning: one last run wherever the snow is (Teine night session? Kamui again?), return the van at New Chitose, fly home. Ten days, one island, two missions — see you at the next one.

blocks.title: Wrap up
blocks.description: Return the van clean-ish, dump gear, last onigiri at the konbini. Debrief on the plane: which storm day wins?
